title: Manager ask runway — 15min rehearsal (Marta Ruiz)
body:
Purpose

Quick rehearsal notes for a 15-minute manager sync where I land a 2-part ask: (1) alignment on promotion runway for two ICs, (2) a short pilot for manager calibration workshops. This is a compact script + evidence ledger + fallback asks. Use as a one-page prompt before the meeting.

Key framing (30s opener)
- Thanks for time — quick status check then 2 asks that map to retention and ramping costs.
- TL;DR: two promotion-ready trajectories (summary + evidence), and a 6-week manager calibration pilot to reduce bias and speed decisions.

Structure (15 minutes)
- 0:00–01:00 - Opening + agenda (explicit ask to block 15m).
- 01:00–05:00 - Candidate A summary + 3 signal bullets (metrics + impact + examples).
- 05:00–09:00 - Candidate B summary + 3 signal bullets.
- 09:00–12:00 - Ask 1: promotion runway recommendation + desired decision window.
- 12:00–14:00 - Ask 2: 6-week calibration pilot ask + low-friction pilot design.
- 14:00–15:00 - Quick commitment from manager + next steps.

Candidate A (Sahil) — condensed evidence (use this script)
- Role: Principal People Partner (IC3 -> IC4 trajectory).
- Impact: led cross-functional hiring playbook that cut time-to-hire from 42->29 days (core metric).
- Qualitative: coached two managers who later promoted; feedback excerpts: "turns messy feedback into concrete plans".
- Risk notes: needs clearer ROI story for org-level change; propose 3-month advisory slot to surface program metrics.
- Ask: greenline for formal promotion packet prep now, target decision in 6–8 weeks.

Candidate B (Ava) — condensed evidence
- Role: Senior People Ops (IC2 -> IC3).
- Impact: launched onboarding revamp, new first-30-day NPS +12 pts; adoption at 80% of hires.
- Qualitative: consistently rated top for cross-team influence in skip-level feedback.
- Risk notes: needs more documented scope growth examples; propose pairing with product PM for 8-week project to close gap.
- Ask: start promotion readiness packet and fast-track to peer calibration in next cycle.

Manager calibration pilot (Ask 2) — elevator pitch
- Problem: inconsistent calibration conversations slow promotions and create perceived unfairness.
- Pilot: 6 weeks, cohort of 6 managers, two 60-minute workshops (bias awareness + evidence triage), one live mock calibration, and a short rubric we adopt for the cycle.
- Success signals: reduced review rework by 30% in pilot cohort, faster decision windows, clearer action items for candidates.
- Low friction: we (People Ops) run materials, one engineering partner (Noah) volunteers 1 hour of customer of the process. Budget ~4–6 hours of effort per manager.
- Ask: greenlight pilot and commit a 6–8 week decision horizon to evaluate.

Fallback asks (if manager hesitates)
- Minimal: Commit to a one-hour discovery with top-of-funnel stakeholders and a decision to run a paid 1-run workshop.
- Alternative: Approve promotion packet work now and defer pilot decision to next leadership sync.

Measurement & follow-ups (what I'll deliver if we get a yes)
- Week 0: send candidate packet templates + short evidence checklist (2 pages).
- Week 2: draft promotion narratives and stakeholder list.
- Pilot kickoff: workshop materials, schedule, and rubric; short post-pilot report.

Quick rebut scripts (if pushback on headcount/time)
- On headcount: "The pilot is designed to re-use manager time more effectively; if we speed promotions for two people we offset future hiring needs and reduce recruiter cycles."
- On evidence overhead: "We provide tight templates — one page per candidate — and we manage collection so managers only need to confirm and add color."

Evidence ledger (copy-paste-able bullets to paste in meeting)
- Sahil: time-to-hire down 31% after playbook; 2 promoted managers coached (names + dates); 3 stakeholder quotes in Slack thread #hiring-ops (ref link).
- Ava: onboarding NPS +12, 80% adoption rate (dashboard link), top quartile in skip-level feedback for Q4.

Notes-to-self for tone and pacing
- Be concise: speak in metric + evidence + proposal order.
- Mirror manager language: if they ask about cost, use hiring/recruiter-cycle framing.
- Pause after each candidate summary to let manager react.

Open questions I want committed to in meeting
- Decision window for promotions (6–8 weeks?)
- Manager volunteers for pilot cohort (names)
- Any stakeholders to include in packet review (skip-levels, eng PMs?)

Quick checklist before 1:1 (10 minutes prep)
- Pull latest hiring dashboard links + one-sentence metric for each candidate.
- Draft two one-pagers (candidate packet starter).
- Slack thread with sample stakeholder quotes and link to pilot one-pager.
- Calendar invite with 15 minutes and an explicit agenda line.

Post-meeting commit template (to paste into thread)
- Thanks — recap: agreed asks: 1) promotion packet for Sahil and Ava (target decision 6–8w), 2) greenlight for 6-week calibration pilot. Next steps: I will send packets by EOD Fri and draft pilot plan.

Bottom line (30-second close)
- Two near-term promotions reduce hire pressure and signal growth; a short calibration pilot buys consistency and speeds future pathways. Both are low-cost with measurable upside.

Scratch:
- If this goes sideways, propose an experimental "fast-track memo" that documents candidate work and timelines to reduce ambiguity.
- Keep this file as my one-page pre-meeting ritual. Update evidence bullets with links prior to the meeting.
